Registry sample second review

Darknode CLI 2.46.1: BENIGN.
SHA256 7fb5fd92c527308f4e94e7e6f3e3e0576ef1a09d20b42ae63990707823dcf099

The package implements the advertised security console and coding agent. Its
postinstall script only checks opt-out/CI variables, prints setup hints, and
exits. darknode.js imports toolkit/revshell.js; menuShell and the revshell CLI
print its returned command strings. The API payload-generation handler returns
a payload/listener object. Those paths do not execute the generated shells.
The methodology, exploit, AD, threat-intelligence, and compliance modules are
reference tables, sometimes with pure search/format helpers. The pentest engine
can execute operator-selected assessment commands; authorization and deployment
context still matter. Dangerous documented capabilities alone do not establish
an implant. No deployment evidence was supplied that would establish misuse.

The named npm update is a normal npm self-update path: compare versions, then
spawn npm install when applying an update. Downloaded 2.46.2 matches both
supplied SHA1 and SHA512 checksums. Its postinstall, revshell builder, and
methodology table are byte-identical to 2.46.1. The shared execution
paths support the same tool identification.

Corrections distinguish reference data and code generation from active calls.
A host-language AST observation requires described records or string-array
tables and rejects imports, unknown calls,
constructors outside the pure-helper vocabulary, and parse errors. It is
file-scoped and is not a package-name allowlist. Executed TCP shell templates
retain a separate child-process-import plus execution-call detection. Shell
variables in non-JavaScript sources are not treated as JS interpolations.
Base64-recovered PHP snippets retain request and system-call capability facts;
standalone PHP shells and executing encoded PHP loaders retain their attack
coverage. The archive-wide postinstall/Git-hook conjunction was retired because
it joined an install hint to an unrelated manual bootstrap implementation.

Domain normalizer archive: MALICIOUS.
SHA256 41f40da0d950b1137dece39acf460f3b528c1f22c0e8c03e736cba0dd7aa66c6

The Go functions genuinely normalize/parse domains, but README download and
example links redirect users to bundled Windows launchers. Launcher.bat starts
lua.exe sync.log; LaunchApp.bat starts init.exe icon.txt. The former PE imports
LuaJIT/lua51.dll APIs including luaL_loadfile and lua_pcall. The script arguments
are obscured Lua, not domain data. Decimal escapes, numeric dispatch state,
indexed string reassembly, and encrypted strings obscure the implementation.
Cleave's recovered source resolves real property lookups and command assembly.
The code builds a hidden elevated PowerShell Start-Process invocation with
Add-MpPreference exclusions for the system drive and executable extensions. It
also builds daily schtasks commands with named actions and scheduled-task
registration, and contains WinInet request/response and DLL execution paths.
This is executable loader/persistence behavior unrelated to domain parsing.

A restricted Lua interpreter with no native modules, filesystem, network, or
process access independently reached require('ffi') in both bundled scripts.
A second instrumented run supplied only inert FFI/bit stubs, recovered native
API declarations/module loading, and stopped at GetConsoleWindow. Native calls
were never allowed. The AV-bypass and task claims are supported by recovered
command construction and corresponding dispatch paths, not merely scores.
Existing Defender-bypass and task-persistence hostile detections remain accurate.
The remote final payload and actual victim deployment are unknown; they are not
needed to explain the deceptive launcher, protection bypass, and persistence.

Email origin chain archive: MALICIOUS.
SHA256 4f13f5343fc56c07c3ee3dd9d184c1bc7ed6882c3e31e36baea4a1578b2ce4a7

src/index.ts exports the advertised MIME/inline email parser, then immediately
executes appended top-level code. Its selector decoder maps FE00..FE0F and
E0100..E01EF to bytes, then evals the recovered UTF-8 source. Decoding 9,123
selectors yields a generator that initializes AES-256-CBC with a literal key
and IV, combines cipher.update and cipher.final into one variable, and yields
eval of that variable. Offline OpenSSL decryption recovered the next stage.
Array spread drains the generator immediately; yielding a timer promise does
not defer evaluation until that promise resolves.

The decrypted stage schedules a ten-second callback, checks Russian locale and
time-zone information, and consults a home-directory init.json date guard. It
queries Solana getSignaturesForAddress through several RPC providers, polls for
a memo, parses memo JSON, base64-decodes its link, and fetches that URL with an
OS header. It obtains response headers for IV/key material and executes the
response after base64 decoding, directly on macOS or in a Node VM context with
require/process access on other platforms. The VM is not a security boundary.
No live RPC endpoint or payload URL was contacted. The actual final response
is unknown, so credential theft is not asserted. Hidden import-time remote-code
execution, geofencing, and throttling decisively contradict an email parser.

Trait placement and coverage

Variation-selector byte arithmetic moved from supply-chain objectives to
micro-behaviors/data/decode/custom. Range checks moved to data/string/unicode.
The manifest's eval(Buffer.from) text is source call syntax metadata. The
redundant decoded-buffer union was expanded at its consumers. Unicode execution
concealment moved from supply-chain/code-metric categories to steganography;
its weaker non-ASCII/invisible/eval co-occurrence is suspicious, not proof that
most bytes are invisible. A stronger hostile variant additionally requires a
real invisible-byte decoder, preserving the zero-width loader control. A new generator rule binds the same cipher receiver
and plaintext variable through update, final, and eval, covering the payload
path missed by the existing value-flow rule.

Function-name-only decryptPayload evidence and START-variable command text
moved to source metadata. Mimikatz command text is source syntax, not the
identity of the artifact. SQL xp_cmdshell invocation is a neutral shell
capability. Bash/Zsh history command text is a neutral file-read observation,
without an invented QNX restriction. The LD_PRELOAD profile-write rule now
requires one write call with a profile target and LD_PRELOAD content; neighboring
forensic path descriptions do not establish a write. Hashcat mode matching now
requires the -m option, and inert tables do not establish cracking activity.
Exact consumers of relocated rules were updated. The lost ancestor memberships
were unsupported capability/identity inferences from syntax and are intentional
corrections. Existing matching scopes otherwise remain explicit in the rules.

Validation controls

check.py scans inert fixtures without executing them. The 23 controls cover
literal/multiline tables, a table with real process execution, generated versus
executed TCP shell templates, non-JS shell variables, standalone/encoded PHP
shells, linked/unrelated cipher-eval variables, forensic descriptions versus
actual profile writes, declaration-only evidence, manifest syntax, selector
arithmetic, an archive with separate install and manual-bootstrap actions, three benign
brand/account/vendor controls, and a concealed zero-width execution control.
Run: python3 testdata/taxonomy/registry-review/check.py --scratch <directory>

Final archive rescans retain zero hostile and one suspicious finding for
Darknode (including 2.46.2), two hostile detections in the domain archive, and three in the email archive.
The retained Darknode suspicious finding describes its real SQL SLEEP probe.
No external malware feed, advisory, or scanner verdict was used as corroboration.

Judgement marker lines (commit-body text):
Darknode CLI: benign toolkit; fixed inert-reference false positives
Domain normalizer: malicious Lua AV bypass and task persistence
Email origin chain: hidden remote-code loader; added decrypt/eval trait
